title: Consumer complaints: filter then rank by urgency
prompt: Find complaints about charges continuing after cancellation or unauthorized recurring charges, then rank by urgency.
notes: The full 5,000-row demo sample (8 of the 15 columns) so the one-shot request stays under the 272K-token long-context tier; the 100,000-row file used in the walkthrough is ~6,783,860 tokens and cannot be sent to gpt-6-astra in one request at all.

The 2026 CFPB export has no free-text narratives; both approaches judge the Product / Issue / Sub-issue text, so matches are rare. There is no gold label; 169 rows carry a topical keyword (unauthorized / cancel / recurring / continuing / can't stop withdrawals) and the share of selected rows carrying one is reported only as a sanity check.

questions.name: recurring_charge
questions.instruction: The text may be in any language; judge its meaning. Does this complaint describe charges continuing after the customer cancelled a service, subscription, or account, OR unauthorized charges and/or unwanted recurring (subscription/membership) charges being made without the customer's consent? Treat any phrasing that implies one of these (e.g. 'they kept billing me after I cancelled', 'I never signed up for this', 'unauthorized transactions', 'charge recurs every month despite cancellation') as satisfying the condition.

criteria.true: The complaint is about: (a) charges/billing continuing after the customer cancelled or attempted to cancel, or (b) charges the customer did not authorize, or (c) recurring/subscription/membership charges the customer does not want or never agreed to. Implied statements count as evidence.
criteria.false: The complaint is about something else, e.g. disputes over a single purchase, fees or interest, credit report errors, debt collection, trouble opening/closing/activating an account, or payment processing problems, without any cancelled-but-still-charged, unauthorized, or unwanted recurring charge element.

questions.name: urgency_score
questions.instruction: Rate how urgent this complaint is for prioritized handling. Complaints where money is still actively being taken after cancellation or repeatedly without consent are most urgent; historical or one-off occurrences are less urgent.
levels: Low urgency: historical, minor, or one-off issue with little indication of ongoing financial harm.
Moderate urgency: unauthorized or unwanted recurring charges occurred, but the ongoing status is unclear or appears isolated.
High urgency: charges are still actively recurring or continuing after cancellation, or repeated unauthorized charges suggest immediate ongoing financial harm to the consumer.

plan.title: Find post-cancellation / unauthorized recurring charge complaints and rank by urgency
plan.description: Filters complaints to those where charges continued after the customer cancelled or unauthorized/recurring charges occurred, then scores each matching complaint for urgency and ranks them most urgent first. Adjust the urgency rubric levels or the true_min threshold if you want a broader/narrower match set.
